212.text: Do not now, because thou hearest that He sitteth, suppose that His being called High Priest is mere idle talk. For the former, viz. His sitting, belongs to the dignity of the Godhead, but this to His great lovingkindness, and His tender care for us.
212.author: St. John Chrysostom
212.work: Homilies on the Epistle to the Hebrews, Homily 14

213.text: It follows then that our things are in Heaven, and heavenly things are ours, even though they be accomplished on earth; since although angels are on earth, yet they are called Heavenly.
213.author: St. John Chrysostom
213.work: Homilies on the Epistle to the Hebrews, Homily 16

214.text: Do we not make allowances for ourselves most of all? If we were thus disposed towards our neighbors also, there will never be any remembrance of injuries.
214.author: St. John Chrysostom
214.work: Homilies on the Epistle to the Hebrews, Homily 19

215.text: If therefore we wish to obtain all good things, let us seek the things of God. For as they who seek the things of this world fail both of them and of the others, so they who prefer the things of God, obtain both.
215.author: St. John Chrysostom
215.work: Homilies on the Epistle to the Hebrews, Homily 26

216.text: Let us persuade ourselves that we have sinned. Let us say it not with the tongue only, but also with the mind. Let us not call ourselves sinners, but also count over our sins, going over them each specifically.
216.author: St. John Chrysostom
216.work: Homilies on the Epistle to the Hebrews, Homily 31

217.text: Let us then stretch our mind towards Heaven, let us be held fast by that desire, let us clothe ourselves with spiritual fire, let us gird ourselves with its flame.
217.author: St. John Chrysostom
217.work: Homilies on the Epistle to the Hebrews, Homily 34

231.text: Thy life hath not yet shone in perfect brightness, because there are sins in thee; but yet thou hast already begun to be enlightened, because there is in thee the confession of sins.
231.author: St. Augustine
231.work: Homilies on the First Epistle of John, Homily I

232.text: Be not thou a liar, to profess one thing and do another; keep thou the faith, and He keeps His promise. But if thou keep not the faith, thine own self, not He that promised, hath defrauded thee.
232.author: St. Augustine
232.work: Homilies on the First Epistle of John, Homily IV

233.text: Let him question his own heart. If he love his brother the Spirit of God dwelleth in him. Let him see, let him prove himself before the eyes of God, let him see whether there be in him the love of peace and unity, the love of the Church that is spread over the whole earth.
233.author: St. Augustine
233.work: Homilies on the First Epistle of John, Homily VI

234.text: Could we love Him, unless He first loved us? If we were slow to love, let us not be slow to love in return. He first loved us; not even so do we love.
234.author: St. Augustine
234.work: Homilies on the First Epistle of John, Homily VII

235.text: Do thou love, and that with a brotherly love: he is not yet a brother, but thou lovest to the end he may be a brother. Well then, all our love is a brotherly love, towards Christians, towards all His members.
235.author: St. Augustine
235.work: Homilies on the First Epistle of John, Homily X

239.text: Doubtless on account of its rising and setting, and rising again, that He was born and suffered and rose again, therefore the Scripture gave this similitude, likening His face to the glory of the sun.
239.author: St. Victorinus of Pettau

240.text: The hidden manna is immortality; the white gem is adoption to be the son of God; the new name written on the stone is "Christian."
240.author: St. Victorinus of Pettau

241.text: The habit of saints is set forth; of those, to wit, who are lowly in the world, and unskilled in the Scriptures, and who hold the faith immoveably, and are not at all broken down by any chance, or withdrawn from the faith by any fear.
241.author: St. Victorinus of Pettau

242.text: The burning torches of fire signify the gift of the Holy Spirit, that it is given by the wood of the passion.
242.author: St. Victorinus of Pettau

243.text: For He is called a lion for the overcoming of death; but for the suffering for men He was led as a lamb to the slaughter.
243.author: St. Victorinus of Pettau

244.text: For after the Lord ascended into heaven and opened all things, He sent the Holy Spirit, whose words the preachers sent forth as arrows reaching to the human heart, that they might overcome unbelief.
244.author: St. Victorinus of Pettau

245.text: We must not regard the order of what is said, because frequently the Holy Spirit, when He has traversed even to the end of the last times, returns again to the same times, and fills up what He had before failed to say.
245.author: St. Victorinus of Pettau

246.text: If by any means, even in the last times, any one should be willing to be converted, any one might even still be saved.
246.author: St. Victorinus of Pettau

248.text: To be sweet in the mouth is the reward of the preaching of the speaker, and is most pleasant to the hearers; but it is most bitter both to those that announce it, and to those that persevere in its commandments through suffering.
248.author: St. Victorinus of Pettau

249.text: The temple opened is a manifestation of our Lord. For the temple of God is the Son, as He Himself says: "Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up."
249.author: St. Victorinus of Pettau

250.text: Moreover, being clothed with the sun intimates the hope of resurrection and the glory of the promise.
250.author: St. Victorinus of Pettau

253.text: That is, that they stood stedfastly in the faith upon their baptism, and having their confession in their mouth, that they shall exult in the kingdom before God.
253.author: St. Victorinus of Pettau

257.text: The horse, and He that sits upon him, sets forth our Lord coming to His kingdom with the heavenly army.
257.author: St. Victorinus of Pettau

258.text: the devil, excluded from the hearts of believers, began to take possession of the wicked, in whose hearts, blinded day by day, he is shut up as if in a profound abyss.
258.author: St. Victorinus of Pettau

259.text: I say, in respect of the square city, he shows forth the united multitude of the saints, in whom the faith could by no means waver.
259.author: St. Victorinus of Pettau

1.text: Whoso is in the law, acteth according to the law; whoso is under the law, is acted upon according to the law: the one therefore is free, the other a slave.
1.author: St. Augustine
1.work: Expositions on the Book of Psalms, Psalm 1

2.text: Now God is said to turn away His face, when He doth not give to the soul, which as yet hath not the pure eye of the mind, the knowledge of Himself.
2.author: St. Augustine
2.work: Expositions on the Book of Psalms, Psalm 12

3.text: For from the head of this Psalm are the words, which He cried out, whilst hanging on the Cross, sustaining also the person of the old man, whose mortality He bare.
3.author: St. Augustine
3.work: Expositions on the Book of Psalms, Psalm 21

4.text: To Thy power I commend My Spirit, soon to receive It back.
4.author: St. Augustine
4.work: Expositions on the Book of Psalms, Psalm 30

5.text: Be humble if thou wouldest bless the Lord at all times, and that His praise should be ever in thy mouth
5.author: St. Augustine
5.work: Expositions on the Book of Psalms, Psalm 33

6.text: Long thou for this light: for a certain fountain, a certain light, such as thy bodily eyes know not; a light to see which the inward eye must be prepared; a fountain, to drink of which the inward thirst is to be kindled.
6.author: St. Augustine
6.work: Expositions on the Book of Psalms, Psalm 41

7.text: He that imploreth great mercy, confesseth great misery.
7.author: St. Augustine
7.work: Expositions on the Book of Psalms, Psalm 50

8.text: Here we must thirst, in another place we shall be filled.
8.author: St. Augustine
8.work: Expositions on the Book of Psalms, Psalm 62

9.text: When God blesseth us, we grow, and when we bless the Lord, we grow, to us both are profitable.
9.author: St. Augustine
9.work: Expositions on the Book of Psalms, Psalm 66

10.text: When were the feet moved, except when the heart was not right?
10.author: St. Augustine
10.work: Expositions on the Book of Psalms, Psalm 72

11.text: If thou hast thy own house, thou art poor; if God's, thou art rich.
11.author: St. Augustine
11.work: Expositions on the Book of Psalms, Psalm 83

12.text: Observe whether he teaches anything but this, that all our trust be in God, none in man.
12.author: St. Augustine
12.work: Expositions on the Book of Psalms, Psalm 90

13.text: In proportion as the wound was deeper in their own hearts, with the greater eagerness did they seek for a physician.
13.author: St. Augustine
13.work: Expositions on the Book of Psalms, Psalm 94

14.text: We sung as much as sufficed for the time, and were then silent: ought our hearts within us to be silent to the blessing of the Lord?
14.author: St. Augustine
14.work: Expositions on the Book of Psalms, Psalm 102

15.text: For His mercy is not for a time, so as not to be for ever, since for this purpose His present mercy is over men, that they may live with the Angels for ever.
15.author: St. Augustine
15.work: Expositions on the Book of Psalms, Psalm 106

16.text: We know that Christ sitteth at the right hand of the Father, since His resurrection from the dead, and ascent into heaven.
16.author: St. Augustine
16.work: Expositions on the Book of Psalms, Psalm 109

17.text: For to examine into the testimonies of the Lord, and to seek Him with all the heart, this is to be undefiled in the way, this is to walk in the law of the Lord.
17.author: St. Augustine
17.work: Expositions on the Book of Psalms, Psalm 118

18.text: Because He who came to absolve from sins, gave hope even to the sinner down in the deep.
18.author: St. Augustine
18.work: Expositions on the Book of Psalms, Psalm 129

19.text: Prayer then, purely directed from a faithful heart, riseth like incense from a hallowed altar.
19.author: St. Augustine
19.work: Expositions on the Book of Psalms, Psalm 140

20.text: The subject of our meditation in this present life should be the praises of God; for the everlasting exaltation of our life hereafter will be the praise of God, and none can become fit for the life hereafter, who hath not practised himself for it now.
20.author: St. Augustine
20.work: Expositions on the Book of Psalms, Psalm 148

1.text: Whereunto there is this worst addition, that the tongue of many like him abets him, since there are many who magnify with their praises these very misdeeds; whence it comes to pass that the fault is continually growing, nourished by applauses.
1.author: St. Gregory the Dialogist
1.work: Morals on the Book of Job

2.text: Since wisdom lieth not on the surface of things, for it is deep in the unseen.
2.author: St. Gregory the Dialogist
2.work: Morals on the Book of Job

3.text: the very sharpness of the correction becomes the source of light
3.author: St. Gregory the Dialogist
3.work: Morals on the Book of Job

4.text: The entrance to the mind then must be fortified with the whole sum of virtue, lest at any time enemies with insidious intent penetrate into it by the opening of heedless thought.
4.author: St. Gregory the Dialogist
4.work: Morals on the Book of Job

5.text: For on this account I take all this trouble, that ye may have no experience of that honey, for it straightway turns into gall.
5.author: St. John Chrysostom
5.work: Homilies on the First Epistle to the Thessalonians

6.text: Therefore each one of the Elect, when he is oppressed with the sleep of sin, strives to rise to keep the watch of righteousness.
6.author: St. Gregory the Dialogist
6.work: Morals on the Book of Job

7.text: For because the stupidity of the fool is represented by the title of an ox, Solomon says rightly, he goeth after her straightway, as an ox goeth to the slaughter.
7.author: St. Gregory the Dialogist
7.work: Morals on the Book of Job

8.text: For not to know is only ignorance, to refuse to learn is pride.
8.author: St. Gregory the Dialogist
8.work: Morals on the Book of Job

9.text: And ‘He set forth His table,’ i.e. Holy Writ, which with the bread of the word refreshes us when we are wearied, and come to Him away from the burthens of the world, and by its effect of refreshing strengthens us against our adversaries.
9.author: St. Gregory the Dialogist
9.work: Morals on the Book of Job

10.text: so long as anyone lets himself out in words, the gravity of silence being gone, he parts with the safe keeping of the soul.
10.author: St. Gregory the Dialogist
10.work: Morals on the Book of Job

11.text: It often happens that the anger, which is pent up within the heart from silence, burns the more fiercely, and silently frames clamorous speeches, presents to itself words, by which to have its wrath exasperated, and as if set in judgment on the case, answers in exasperation exceeding cruelly
11.author: St. Gregory the Dialogist
11.work: Morals on the Book of Job

12.text: But, on the other hand, whoever is rooted in the desire of eternity alone, is neither uplifted by good fortune nor shaken by adverse fortune; whilst he has nought in the world which he desires, there is nought which he dreads from the world.
12.author: St. Gregory the Dialogist
12.work: Morals on the Book of Job

13.text: For it is plain to all persons that desire, when deferred, is in every case a pain
13.author: St. Gregory the Dialogist
13.work: Morals on the Book of Job

14.text: For when envy has made the mind corrupt, it consumes all that it may have found done aright.
14.author: St. Gregory the Dialogist
14.work: Morals on the Book of Job

15.text: By Anger life is lost, even though wisdom seem to be retained
15.author: St. Gregory the Dialogist
15.work: Morals on the Book of Job

16.text: What then is specially to be observed in all this, but that those who are about to rise, think themselves low, and that they who are soon to fall, ever stand on high ground?
16.author: St. Gregory the Dialogist
16.work: Morals on the Book of Job

17.text: for good men check precipitancy of speech with the reins of counsel, and they take heedful thought, lest, by giving a loose to the wantonness of the tongue, they should by heedlessness of speech pierce their hearer’s spirits
17.author: St. Gregory the Dialogist
17.work: Morals on the Book of Job

18.text: For he that does not regulate his feelings by the reason that is proper to man, must needs live alone like a beast.
18.author: St. Gregory the Dialogist
18.work: Morals on the Book of Job

19.text: But to the more imperfect, this is what we may say, Give of what you have unto the needy.
19.author: St. John Chrysostom
19.work: Homilies on the First Epistle to the Corinthians

20.text: whilst the grace of heavenly visitation illumines us, it discloses even all the depths of the mind that are hidden from our sight.
20.author: St. Gregory the Dialogist
20.work: Morals on the Book of Job

21.text: For His works are so great, that by every thing that is done by man, His Will is sought out; for it often happens that it is done by the very act, whereby it was thought to be thrown aside.
21.author: St. Gregory the Dialogist
21.work: Morals on the Book of Job

22.text: For what he begins badly, he is daily strengthening for the worse by custom.
22.author: St. Gregory the Dialogist
22.work: Morals on the Book of Job

23.text: And whilst they make for that which they are unable to comprehend, they neglect to acquaint themselves with those things, by which they might have been instructed.
23.author: St. Gregory the Dialogist
23.work: Morals on the Book of Job

24.text: For he rightly builds the house of his mind, who first cleanses the field of his body from the thorns of vices
24.author: St. Gregory the Dialogist
24.work: Morals on the Book of Job

25.text: For with more profit to herself she is anxious not to know things she is unable to fathom, rather than boldly to define things she does not know.
25.author: St. Gregory the Dialogist
25.work: Morals on the Book of Job

26.text: He then that letteth out water is a beginning of brawls, for he who neglects to refrain his tongue, dissipates concord.
26.author: St. Gregory the Dialogist
26.work: Morals on the Book of Job

27.text: For silver and gold if it be refuse is consumed by the fire, but if proof, it is brought out by the fire.
27.author: St. Gregory the Dialogist
27.work: Morals on the Book of Job

28.text: For to put the mouth to labour is to employ it in the confession of sin done, but the righteous man doth ‘not refrain his mouth,’ in that forestalling the wrath of the searching Judge, he falls wroth upon himself in words of self-confession.
28.author: St. Gregory the Dialogist
28.work: Morals on the Book of Job

30.text: And they for this reason get to the depths of understanding, because they do not scorn to practise even the very least things that they have learnt, and while they aid the understanding with the hands, they lift themselves above the level of the clever.
30.author: St. Gregory the Dialogist
30.work: Morals on the Book of Job

31.text: For as the entrance of a city is called the ‘gate,’ so is the day of Judgment the gate of the Kingdom, since all the Elect go in thereby to the glory of their heavenly country.
31.author: St. Gregory the Dialogist
31.work: Morals on the Book of Job

1.text: And he calleth him "old," on purpose to show his deformity, and hideousness, and imbecility; and "new," as if to say, Do not expect that it will be with this one even as with the other, but the reverse: for ever as he farther advances, he hasteneth not on to old age, but to a youthfulness greater than the preceding.
1.author: St. John Chrysostom
1.work: Homilies on the Epistle to the Colossians, Homily 8

2.text: For so have we heard, that "a certain Man made a great supper." Who is this Man, but "the Mediator between God and men, the Man Christ Jesus"?
2.author: St. Augustine

3.text: And he says not "revealed," but, "preached the Gospel," to signify that the patriarch was in joy at this method of justification, and in great desire for its accomplishment.
3.author: St. John Chrysostom

4.text: For what good was there in wishing to learn, whether there be many or few that be saved? What benefit resulted from it to the hearers? On the contrary it was a necessary and valuable thing to know in what way a man may attain to salvation.
4.author: St. Cyril of Alexandria

7.text: I mean for instance, a man has been circumcised upon the eighth day; this is circumcision of the flesh: a man has done all the Law bids him; this is circumcision of the mind which St. Paul requires above all, yea rather the Law also.
7.author: St. John Chrysostom
7.work: Homilies on the Epistle to the Romans

8.text: He enjoined things that were in contradiction to the promises, and yet not even so did the righteous man stagger, nor say he had been deceived.
8.author: St. John Chrysostom
8.work: Homilies on the Epistle to the Hebrews, Homily 25

9.text: For the Lord did not seek among men nobility of race, but suitably chose to be born of captives and of sinners, as He came to preach remission of sin to the captives.
9.author: St. Ambrose
9.work: Catena Aurea on Matthew (in Luc., cap. 2)

10.text: Because Nathanael had considered the writings of the Prophets more than Philip. For he had heard from the Scriptures, that Christ must come from Bethlehem, and from the village in which David was.
10.author: St. John Chrysostom
10.work: Homilies on the Gospel of John

11.text: For as in royal palaces, prisoners and those who have offended the king, stand without, and he who desires to reconcile them, does not bring them in, but himself going out discourses with them, until having made them meet for the king's presence, he may bring them in, so also Christ hath done.
11.author: St. John Chrysostom
11.work: Homilies on the Epistle to the Hebrews, Homily 3

13.text: He that was a Greek, or Jew, or bond-man yesterday, carries about with him the form, not of an Angel or Archangel, but of the Lord of all, yea displays in his own person the Christ.
13.author: St. John Chrysostom

14.text: For though He is the Only-begotten as regards His divinity, yet as having become our brother, He has also the name of Firstborn; that, being made the first-fruits as it were of the adoption of men, He might make us also the sons of God.
14.author: St. Cyril of Alexandria

16.text: See how he lifts up their minds, and shows the great honor which God has for us, since He has assigned to Angels who are above us this ministration on our behalf.
16.author: St. John Chrysostom
16.work: Homilies on the Epistle to the Hebrews, Homily 3

17.text: One and the same Christ is preached, when of perfect age, by Apostles; when an infant, and not yet able to speak, is announced by a star to the Gentiles; for so the order of reason required; speaking preachers proclaimed a speaking Lord, mute signs proclaimed a mute infant.
17.author: St. Gregory the Great
17.work: Catena Aurea on Matthew (Hom. in Ev. Lib. i. Hom. 10)

18.text: Listen to the Prophet too, calling him “The Messenger of great counsel.” (Isa. ix. 6.) “The Messenger of great counsel,” is He not great Himself? “The mighty God,” is He small and not great?
18.author: St. John Chrysostom
18.work: Homilies on the Epistle to the Philippians

19.text: He knows what tribulation is; He knows what temptation is, not less than we who have suffered, for He Himself also has suffered.
19.author: St. John Chrysostom
19.work: Homilies on the Epistle to the Hebrews, Homily 5

20.text: See how immediately on His birth the tyrant is furious against Him, and the mother with her Child is driven into foreign lands. So should you in the beginning of your spiritual career seem to have tribulation, you need not to be discouraged, but bear all things manfully, having this example.
20.author: St. John Chrysostom

21.text: What ear is worthy to hear such a tale? How earnestly the soul should prepare itself to receive such high lessons! How pure it should be from carnal affections, how unclouded by worldly disquietudes, how active and ardent in its researches, how eager to find in its surroundings an idea of God which may be worthy of Him!
21.author: St. Basil the Great

23.text: But no man ever possessed all the operations of the Holy Spirit at once, except the sole Mediator between God and man, [1 Tim. 2, 5] Whose is the same Spirit, Who proceedeth from the Father before all ages.
23.author: St. Gregory the Dialogist
23.work: Morals on the Book of Job

25.text: Had not we been first made sons, we could not have called Him Father.
25.author: St. John Chrysostom
